name: What is the best way to design an outdoor kitchen with a pool area?

mainEntity.name: How should an outdoor kitchen be laid out near a pool so it is functional and safe?
mainEntity.text: How should an outdoor kitchen be laid out near a pool so it is functional and safe?

acceptedAnswer.text: An outdoor kitchen works best when it supports the way the backyard will actually be used. In a pool setting, that usually means keeping the cooking zone close enough to the dining area for convenience, but far enough from the pool to avoid crowding, splashing, and wet foot traffic around the grill. The kitchen should be designed with utility runs, ventilation, counter space, sink access, storage, and appliance clearances in mind before the hardscape is built. In Los Angeles, this is especially important because gas, electrical, and drainage routing often needs to be coordinated with the pool, patio, and retaining wall layout. A well-planned kitchen should also consider sun exposure, shade, and seating flow so it feels like part of the whole backyard instead of an isolated add-on. The best time to plan it is during the site design phase, not after the pool is already under construction.
acceptedAnswer.description: An outdoor kitchen should be placed for easy access to the patio and dining area without creating smoke, splash, or traffic conflicts around the pool. Utility lines, ventilation, countertop space, storage, and cleanup flow should all be planned before hardscape is poured.
